# graph-manager: `SpecView` component (Markdown + Mermaid, safe) ## What to build A React component that renders a spec's Markdown text, with ```` ```mermaid ```` blocks drawn as diagrams. It is used by the floating spec pane on the Terminals page (a later task), so it takes the text as a prop and does no fetching. Markdown is rendered with `marked` (GFM); raw HTML in the text is escaped, unsafe links lose their `href`. Mermaid is imported lazily (`await import("mermaid")`) so it ends up in its own Vite chunk, and each block renders on its own: a broken block shows an error and its source, the rest of the spec still renders. `marked@18.1.1` and `mermaid@12.2.0` are already dependencies of `apps/graph-manager` (committed in `package.json` and `package-lock.json`); do not add or upgrade packages. Spec: `docs/prd/graph-manager-spec-view.md` (section "Web: the spec view"). ## Context: files to read before implementing - `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/TaskGraph.tsx` and `TaskGraph.css` — a self-contained presentational component with its own CSS file; mirror the file layout and CSS token use. - `apps/graph-manager/src/web/ui/tokens.css` and `ui/base.css` — the design tokens (colors, fonts, radii) for light and dark; use them, never hard-coded colors. - `apps/graph-manager/src/web/ui/theme.ts` (lines 1-90) — `useTheme()` returns `{ resolved: "light" | "dark" }`; the component takes `theme` as a prop instead so it stays pure. - `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/TaskGraph.test.tsx` — component test style: `// @vitest-environment jsdom` first line, `@testing-library/react` `render`/`screen`/`cleanup`, `vi.mock` for heavy modules. - `apps/graph-manager/vite.config.ts` and `tsconfig.web.json` — the web build; `marked` ships its own types; `mermaid` ships its own types. ## Patterns to follow - Files: `apps/graph-manager/src/web/components/SpecView.tsx`, `SpecView.css`, `SpecView.test.tsx`, plus pure helpers in `apps/graph-manager/src/web/spec.ts` with `spec.test.ts` (node environment, no DOM). - Imports in web code have no `.js` suffix (Vite/bundler resolution), e.g. `import { api } from "../api";`. ## Step-by-step tasks ### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/spec.ts` - **IMPLEMENT** - `export function safeHref(href: string): string | undefined` — keep `http:`/`https:` (case-insensitive), `#…`, and relative paths (no scheme: no `:` before the first `/`, `?` or `#`); everything else (`javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, `file:` …) → undefined. - `export function renderSpecHtml(text: string): string` — a module-level `new Marked({ gfm: true, breaks: false })` with `renderer` overrides (marked 18 token API): - `html(token)` → `escapeHtml(token.text)` (raw HTML, block or inline, shown as text); - `code(token)` → for `token.lang === "mermaid"`: `
${escapeHtml(token.text)}
` (`i` = running index within this render); otherwise `
${escapeHtml(token.text)}
`; - `link(token)` → `safeHref(token.href)`; when undefined, return just the rendered inline text (`this.parser.parseInline(token.tokens)`); when `http(s)` add `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`; escape the href attribute; - `image(token)` → only for `http(s)`/relative srcs, with `loading="lazy"` and escaped `alt`; else the alt text. - `export function mermaidSources(text: string): string[]` — the mermaid block sources in order (from `marked.lexer`, walking tokens for `type === "code" && lang === "mermaid"`), so the component can render block `i` from source `i` (never read it back from the DOM). - `escapeHtml` / `escapeAttr` local helpers (`& < > " '`). - **GOTCHA**: in marked 18 a renderer method receives one token object, and `this` is the renderer (`this.parser`); use `function` syntax, not arrows, for overrides that need `this`. ### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/spec.test.ts` - **IMPLEMENT** (node env): headings/lists/GFM tables render; `` → contains `<script>`, no `` inline → escaped; `[x](javascript:alert(1))` → no `href`; `[x](https://a.b)` → `href="https://a.b"` with `target="_blank"`; `[x](#goal)` and `[x](../a.md)` keep href; mermaid block → `class="spec-mermaid"` with `data-mermaid="0"`, its source escaped (`A-->B`); two mermaid blocks → indexes 0 and 1 and `mermaidSources` returns both sources. ### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/components/SpecView.tsx` and `SpecView.css` - **IMPLEMENT** `export function SpecView({ text, theme }: { text: string; theme: "light" | "dark" })`: - `const html = useMemo(() => renderSpecHtml(text), [text]);` rendered into `
`. - `useEffect` on `[html, theme]`: `const { default: mermaid } = await import("mermaid");` `mermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false, securityLevel: "strict", theme: theme === "dark" ? "dark" : "default" });` then for each `[data-mermaid]` element `i` in `ref.current`: `const { svg } = await mermaid.render(\`spec-mmd-${uid}-${i}\`, sources[i])` (with `uid` from `useId()` sanitized to `[a-z0-9-]`) and set the element's `innerHTML = svg`, adding class `spec-mermaid-ok`; on error set its content to `
Diagram error: 
escaped source
`. Use a cancelled flag so a stale render never writes after a newer one. - CSS: readable document column (`max-width: 860px`), headings, lists, tables (borders with the border token), `pre` with the surface token, `.spec-mermaid` centered and horizontally scrollable, `.spec-mermaid-error` with the danger token. Light and dark come from tokens. ### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/components/SpecView.test.tsx` - **IMPLEMENT** (jsdom): `vi.mock("mermaid", () => ({ default: { initialize: vi.fn(), render: vi.fn(async (_id: string, src: string) => { if (src.includes("BROKEN")) throw new Error("Parse error"); return { svg: "" }; }) } }))`. Assert: heading text visible; a valid mermaid block gets the svg (`await screen.findByTestId("mmd")`); a broken block shows `Diagram error: Parse error` while the valid one still renders; `initialize` called with `securityLevel: "strict"` and `theme: "dark"` for `theme="dark"`; re-rendering with new text replaces the content. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Markdown, tables and code render; raw HTML and unsafe links are neutralized (unit tests). - [ ] Mermaid blocks render to SVG via a lazy import; a broken block shows an error, the others render. - [ ] `npm run build -w graph-manager` emits mermaid in a separate chunk (the main entry chunk does not contain `mermaid`; check `apps/graph-manager/dist/web/assets/`). - [ ] `npm test -w graph-manager -- src/web/spec.test.ts src/web/components/SpecView.test.tsx` passes. ## Validation commands ```bash npm run typecheck && npm run lint npm test -w graph-manager -- src/web/spec.test.ts src/web/components/SpecView.test.tsx npm run build -w graph-execution && npm run build -w graph-manager ```
